questions.q: According to the episode, what TWO jobs does experimentation do when developing a major design project?
options: It records the budget and it schedules the production timeline
It generates ideas, by revealing what materials, tools and technologies can do, and it tests ideas, by trialling whether something actually works
It only confirms decisions the designer has already made on paper
It markets the product and it gathers customer feedback after launch
questions.explanation: Experimentation is hands-on testing of materials, tools and technologies that does two jobs: it generates ideas by showing what a material can do (sparking possibilities you would not imagine on paper) and it tests ideas by trialling whether a joint, finish or mechanism actually performs. It is an engine for both generating and evaluating ideas, not just confirming a decision already made.

questions.q: Which of the following best outlines why designers undertake research and experimentation when developing a product?
options: To avoid making mistakes
To determine the properties of the materials to be used
To ensure all the materials are available for production
To ensure the best tools, materials and techniques are used
questions.explanation: Research and experimentation let the designer test options and select the most appropriate tools, materials and techniques for the product. Determining material properties is only one part of this broader aim.

questions.q: The syllabus skill is to RESPOND to the findings of experimentation and research. In the MDP, what does responding to findings actually mean?
options: Filing the research printouts and test results neatly in the folio
Gathering as much research as possible so the folio looks full
Analysing and evaluating the results and modifying the design accordingly, so the research changes a decision
Repeating each experiment until it confirms the design you already chose
questions.explanation: Research and experimentation only have value when they change a decision. Responding means you analyse and evaluate the results and apply them by modifying the design — the evaluate-and-refine loop. A folio full of research that never changed the design scores poorly; research that visibly drove decisions scores well.

questions.q: Using a variety of research methods in the process of design is important because it
options: helps develop marketing strategies.
improves understanding of customer needs.
promotes the use of emerging technologies.
protects the intellectual property of the designer.
questions.explanation: Using varied research methods triangulates data from different sources, giving the designer a fuller and more reliable understanding of customer needs. The other options are not the central reason for researching during the design process.

questions.q: In developing your MDP, which of the following is an example of PRIMARY research?
options: Reading published material specifications and standards
Surveying your target users about their needs
Looking up an existing product review online
Consulting a textbook on manufacturing techniques
questions.explanation: Primary research is data the designer gathers first-hand for the project, such as surveying target users or conducting material experiments and tests — current and specific to the project. Secondary research, like material specifications, standards or published studies, comes from existing sources others have produced.

questions.q: The episode gives a model folio experiment for choosing a chair-seat material. Which structure makes an experiment worth real marks?
options: A list of materials you considered, with no results
Aim, method, result, and a design decision that responds to the result
A photo of the workshop and a note that testing was done
A conclusion stating which material you preferred from the start
questions.explanation: Document experiments as primary research: a clear aim, a fair (controlled) method, a result, and a design decision that responds to the result. For the chair seat the aim was the most suitable material for strength and comfort, the method loaded three materials identically and recorded deflection, the result was that plywood deflected least with no cracking, and the response was to select plywood and note the evidence.

questions.q: From memory: what two jobs does experimentation do, and what is the most important thing you must do with your findings?
keyPoints: Experimentation generates ideas — by revealing what materials, tools and technologies can do.
Experimentation tests ideas — by trialling whether something actually works.
The most important thing is to RESPOND to the findings: analyse and evaluate the results and apply them by modifying the design.
The trap is gathering research and never using it — research only has value when it changes a decision.
questions.explanation: If you said 'generate and test ideas, then respond to and act on the findings', that is the mark. The verb respond is the whole point.

questions.q: From memory: what is the full research toolkit you apply to the MDP, and what tells you WHAT to research?
keyPoints: The full toolkit is QISOTS — questionnaires, interviews, surveys, observation, tests and experiments, and statistical analysis — from module three.
Plus information research from print and electronic (secondary) sources.
Use both primary research (gathered yourself) and secondary research (from existing sources).
The areas of investigation listed in your project proposal tell you what to research — materials, users, existing products, techniques.
questions.explanation: Research for the MDP is module three's QISOTS turned on your own real project, and your proposal's areas of investigation are the map of what to research. The same ethics (CVA) apply when you research people.

questions.q: Outline how testing and experimenting can improve a design project.
questions.modelAnswer: Testing and experimenting improve a design project by letting the designer explore the successes and failures of different materials, tools and techniques before committing to them. This saves time, money and material wastage and leads to a better-resolved final design.

criteria.descriptor: Outlines relevant information regarding testing and experimenting and how it can improve a design

questions.explanation: A strong answer links testing and experimenting to better decisions: you trial materials, tools and techniques, find what works, and respond to that finding by refining the design. Method, finding, response.

questions.q:
Research is important in the early stages of designing a new product.

Explain the factors a designer would need to consider when interpreting and applying research data.

criteria.descriptor: Makes the relationship between the factors and the consideration evident (when interpreting and applying research data); provides the reasons why the designer considers these factors
Provides characteristics and features of the factors a designer would need to consider when interpreting and applying research data
Sketches in general terms factors a designer would consider when interpreting and applying research data
Identifies a factor a designer would consider when interpreting and applying research data

questions.modelAnswer: When interpreting and applying research data a designer must consider the reliability and validity of the source (primary data the designer gathered versus more general secondary data), the relevance of the data to the project's areas of investigation, and how the data should change the design. Statistical results must be analysed objectively rather than read to confirm a decision already made, and ethical considerations apply when the data comes from people. The designer then applies the findings by modifying the design accordingly, so the research is evidence that drives decisions rather than decoration.
questions.explanation: This question targets the 'respond to findings' skill: it is not enough to collect data — you must interpret it (judging reliability, validity and relevance) and apply it by modifying the design.

questions.q: Describe how research and experimentation informed the development of a major design project.
questions.modelAnswer: To develop my project I used both research and experimentation. Secondary research into material specifications and primary research surveying my target users identified the requirements, and I then experimented to choose between options: for the load-bearing frame I tested three joining methods, loading identical samples and recording strength and deflection. The mortise-and-tenon joint performed best, so I responded to this finding by selecting it for all load-bearing joints and redesigning the corner detail to suit, documenting the experiment and decision in my folio. Similarly, user feedback that the first prototype was too low led me to raise the working height. In each case the research and experimentation produced findings that I analysed and applied, directly shaping the design.

criteria.descriptor: Names specific research and experimentation, states the findings, and clearly shows the design decisions made in response, with evidence
Describes some research and experimentation and links at least one finding to a design decision
Lists research or experimentation activity with little or no link to findings or design decisions

questions.explanation: The headline MDP question. A weak answer lists activity ('I researched materials online and did some experiments'); a strong answer shows method, finding and a design decision that responded to it — method, finding, response, every time. Listing activity without findings or responses caps low.
